title: Sensex, Nifty End Muhurat Trading Lower for First Time in Nine Years
excerpt: The Sensex slipped 28.62 points and the Nifty fell back below 25,000 in Sunday's Diwali session, snapping a seven-day rally as Samvat 2083 began — though smaller stocks rose and investor wealth still grew by Rs 2.60 lakh crore.
body:
• The BSE Sensex closed Sunday's Muhurat session at 80,999.40, down 28.62 points or 0.04%, and the NSE Nifty 50 fell 43.95 points or 0.18% to 24,986.40, slipping back below 25,000.
  • It was the first lower Muhurat close in nine years — the indices last fell in the Diwali session of 2017, after rising in eight straight Muhurat sessions from 2018 to 2025.
  • The dip snapped a seven-day rally in which the Sensex had gained 7,781.99 points, or 10.62% — traders booked profits after the strongest weekly run in more than five years.
  • Smaller stocks moved the other way: the Nifty Smallcap 100 rose 1.00% and investor wealth grew by Rs 2.60 lakh crore. Regular trading resumes Monday, November 9; markets are closed Tuesday, November 10 for Diwali-Balipratipada.

India's stock markets opened the Hindu new year, Samvat 2083, with a small step back. In the one-hour Muhurat trading session held on Diwali afternoon, Sunday, November 8, the Sensex and Nifty closed marginally lower — the first time the ceremonial session has ended in the red since 2017.

The session ran from 2:20 p.m. to 3:30 p.m. IST, in the afternoon slot the exchanges have used for a second consecutive year instead of the traditional evening Lakshmi Puja hour. The Sensex opened higher at 81,299.34 and touched an intraday high of 81,442.11 before profit-taking pulled it to a close of 80,999.40. The Nifty opened at 25,070.45 and closed at 24,986.40. On the Sensex, 16 stocks advanced and 14 declined, according to The Hindu BusinessLine's closing report.

Profit-taking after a record run

The fall came at the end of an exceptional week. Over the previous seven sessions the Sensex had climbed 7,781.99 points, or 10.62%, and the Nifty 2,331.5 points, or 10.27%. On Friday, November 6 alone, the Sensex jumped 1,718.01 points to close at 81,028.02, and the Nifty closed above 25,000 for the first time since February 27. Foreign institutional investors bought Rs 13,749.82 crore of equities on Friday, exchange data showed. Against that run, a flat Muhurat close reads as consolidation rather than a change of direction.

The selling was concentrated in large caps. On the Nifty, SBI Life, InterGlobe Aviation and Bharti Airtel each fell more than 1%; the Sensex laggards included Mahindra & Mahindra, InterGlobe Aviation, Trent, Infosys, Bharti Airtel and Axis Bank. Sun Pharma led the gainers, up 2.96%, followed by ONGC and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles. Tata Steel rose about 3% intraday to Rs 192.19 after reporting a second-quarter net profit of Rs 3,700 crore, up 16% year on year. Broader indices told a different story from the benchmarks: the Nifty Midcap 100 added 0.13%, the Smallcap 100 rose 1.00% and the Microcap 250 gained 1.46%, and total investor wealth rose by Rs 2.60 lakh crore to Rs 5,05,67,743.40 crore.

"After two years of stagnation, market has the potential to give investors bumper returns by next Diwali, because of confluence of low valuation and high earnings growth."

— Raamdeo Agrawal, Chairman and Co-Founder, Motilal Oswal Financial Services

The year that was, and what comes next

The outgoing Samvat 2082 was a losing year for the benchmarks: the Sensex gave up 3,398.32 points, or 4.00%, and the Nifty fell 838.25 points, or 3.24%. That is the backdrop to the nine-year Muhurat statistic — the session that starts the new Samvat had closed higher every year from 2018 through 2025, including a 0.07% Sensex gain on October 21, 2025. The last decline, in 2017, saw the Nifty close 0.63% lower.

Gaurav Garg, head of research at Lemonn, said the direction in the new Samvat would depend on corporate earnings, domestic growth, foreign fund flows, global developments and crude oil movements. Regular trading resumes on Monday, November 9, and the exchanges are closed on Tuesday, November 10 for Diwali-Balipratipada, per the Muhurat trading schedule and market holiday list. For diaspora investors, the practical takeaway is narrow: the headline dip was 0.04% after a 10.6% seven-session rise, and the broader market underneath it was still advancing.
